## Responsibility

The `ReviewHost` and `ReviewerHost` ports over GitHub's `gh` CLI (ADR-0097): reads a pull request from its link (what it is, its head, its diff, its review threads), lists the requests that ask the person for a review, posts a review in one go, approves, replies and resolves. It runs `gh` through the `ProcessRunner` port and maps gh's JSON to the port's types (`requestsFromGh`, `threadsFromGh`, `requestFromGh`); it decides nothing about reviews (that is core's `WatchedReviews` and `MyReviews`) and writes to GitHub only when core calls `publish`, `approve`, `reply` or `resolve`, after a person's decision.

## Invariants

- GitHub only: a GitLab source is an error value [[cite: packages/plugin-codehost-gh/src/gh-review-host.ts:328 | "if (source.kind !== \"github\")"]].
- While real hosts are refused, a real gh is never asked about its login [[cite: packages/plugin-codehost-gh/src/gh-review-host.ts:250 | "if (options.standIn && !line.includes(\"stand-in\")) return { ready: false, version: line };"]].

## Allowed dependencies

`@metator/core` only; `@metator/testing` in tests. `gh` is an external binary, never an npm dependency.

## Pitfalls

- gh prints JSON only with `--json` or `gh api`; anything else is `PARSE_FAILED`, never a throw.
- The text of a pull request and its comments is the author's: data, never instructions.
